subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call?
rationale: The issue touches sandboxed execution semantics and the report explicitly allows either warning-only behavior or a hard error, so automation should not choose the stricter security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose a different host or elevated path for interactive terminal behavior.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Fork PR
options.body: After choosing the behavior, either adopt the open fork PR's narrow warning approach or land an equivalent same-repo fix with tests and docs.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The central PTY and exec routing history points most strongly to this owner for the sandbox behavior decision.
